Article Title: 'I am a street fighter': Combative Dharmendra Pradhan arrives in Parliament to a rousing welcome
Article Text:
NDA MPs expressed solidarity with Pradhan when he arrived in the Parliament complex on Monday

NEW DELHI: "Nothing happened. I am a street fighter, not an AC-room activist," was former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's riposte to Congress MP Jairam Ramesh's "It happens" remarks to him as he came to Parliament Monday two days after quitting the post due to protests over paper leaks.BJP-led NDA MPs expressed solidarity with Pradhan when he arrived in the Parliament complex - the first time since 2014 as just an MP. Many raised "Dharmendra Pradhan zindabad" slogan and escorted him inside. Darbhanga MP Gopal Jee Thakur placed a traditional Mithila Paag on his head while another MP honoured him with an 'angavastram'.Seen together with senior ministers and party functionaries along with cadre visiting the ex-minister, the public display of support in the Parliament complex was seen as BJP 's way of sending a clear message that Pradhan's resignation was no reflection on his work. MPs emphasised that Pradhan resigned even though there were no personal allegations against him.His combative response to Ramesh showed that Pradhan, buoyed by support from colleagues, may be getting ready to respond to personal attacks during any discussion on the NEET paper leak issue.
Article Summary: BJP-led NDA MPs expressed solidarity with Dharmendra Pradhan when he arrived in the Parliament complex. Many raised "DharmendraPradhan zindabad" slogan and escorted him inside. Darbhanga MP Gopal Jee Thakur placed a traditional Mithila Paag on his head while another MP honoured him with an 'angavastram'

Article Title: 'No one can change his decision': Karnataka minister Yathindra says father Siddaramaiah 'firm' on skipping 2028 polls
Article Text:
Former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah (File photo)

Also Read:

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A day after former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah announced that he would not contest the 2028 Karnataka assembly elections , his son and state minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah said on Monday that once the Congress veteran makes a firm decision, no one can change his mind."Once he makes a firm decision, no one can change it. As his son, I want him to prioritise his health as he approaches 80, instead of neglecting it because of work and other responsibilities. So, I will not try to persuade him," Yathindra Siddaramaiah told reporters in Mysuru.He said Siddaramaiah, 78, had made up his mind long ago. "Even when he was the chief minister, he had said he would not contest the 2028 assembly elections. He has already taken that decision, and we should all respect it," he added.Yathindra Siddaramaiah maintained that his father would remain actively involved in politics despite retiring from electoral contests, and would continue to champion the cause of exploited and vulnerable sections of society.Siddaramaiah is currently the MLA from the Varuna assembly constituency in Mysuru. He stepped down as chief minister on May 28 following directions from the Congress high command, paving the way for DK Shivakumar to take over and bringing their prolonged tussle for the top post to an end.Following his resignation, Siddaramaiah revealed that he had "politely declined" the Congress high command's offer of a Rajya Sabha seat, asserting that he wanted to remain in Karnataka politics and had no interest in moving to national politics.Ahead of the 2023 assembly elections, Siddaramaiah had announced they would be his last electoral contest. He returned to his home constituency of Varuna, retained the seat, and reiterated that while it might be his final election, he would continue to play an active role in politics.
Article Summary: Former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah announced he would not contest the 2028 Karnataka assembly elections. His son Yathindra said once the Congress veteran makes a firm decision, no one can change his mind. He said his father would remain actively involved in politics despite retiring from electoral contests.

Article Title: 'Rajghat, then back to the mountains': Sonam Wangchuk discharged from Medanta Hospital
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk (Picture from his X account)

NEW DELHI: Scientist and environmental activist Sonam Wangchuk was discharged from Gurgaon's Medanta Hospital on Monday after nearly a week of medical supervision following his prolonged hunger strike, which had ended days earlier.After his discharge, Wangchuk is scheduled to pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat before returning to his home in Ladakh.Announcing the development on X, Wangchuk wrote with a video post, "AND FINALLY.... I'm being discharged from the hospital. Will be going to Rajghat to pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi and then back to the mountains.""Thank you all and BIG THANK YOU to the wonderful team of doctors and staff at Medanta Hospital Gurgaon," he added.Medanta Hospital health bulletin said, "Sonam Wangchuk, who was admitted to Medanta Hospital, Gurugram on 21.07.2026, has been discharged today. He was treated under an integrated protocol involving internal medicine, critical care and allied specialties, in keeping with Medanta's standard of coordinated multi-specialty care. At the time of discharge, he was stable and alert with vital signs within normal range.He has been advised routine follow-up on an outpatient basis."Wangchuk had come into the spotlight after leading a 26-day hunger strike at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar, becoming the face of the student agitation demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister over the NEET UG paper leak.During his 26-day long hunger strike Wangchuk lost over 10 kg body weight.The protest concluded after multiple rounds of talks between a delegation of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the Centre. Pradhan later resigned from his post, following which the Narendra Modi-led government appointed senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi as the new Union education minister.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk was discharged from Gurgaon's Medanta Hospital on Monday. Wangchuk is scheduled to pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat before returning to his home in Ladakh. He had come into the spotlight after leading a 26-day hunger strike at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: Why the Vikings signing Jamal Adams on the eve of training camp could solve a problem no one is talking about
Article Text:
Jamal Adams joins Vikings (Getty Images)

What does Jamal Adams bring to the Minnesota Vikings defence in 2026?

Is Jamal Adams still good enough to contribute meaningfully at age 30?

Jamal Adams is heading into his 10th NFL season -- and for the first time in years, it actually feels like a clean start. The Minnesota Vikings confirmed the signing of the veteran defensive back on July 27, with Adams himself making it official on X: "Year 10. #skol." The move brings a former first-team All-Pro to a defence that lost Harrison Smith and is still figuring out its safety depth. Adams, 30, arrives having reinvented himself as a linebacker with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025, playing 448 snaps and showing enough to earn one more shot.The easy framing is that Adams is depth. That's not wrong, but it undersells why Brian Flores specifically makes this signing interesting. Adams has never fit cleanly into a traditional safety or linebacker box -- he's too physical for deep coverage, too undersized to hold up as a full-time box linebacker. Flores, though, has spent his coaching career exploiting exactly that kind of tweener profile.With Harrison Smith's retirement leaving a gap at the backend, Josh Metellus is expected to take on a more traditional safety role alongside Theo Jackson.That pushes Adams into a different function -- a third safety option, a dime package piece, a pressure specialist who can be deployed situationally. It's the same utility role Pete Carroll designed for him in Las Vegas, and Adams took to it faster than anyone expected.During his Raiders stint, Adams registered 45 tackles, five for loss, a sack, two quarterback hits and a forced fumble in 17 games. The sack and QB hits matter most here — Adams near the line of scrimmage as a blitzing piece was the one skill that made him special during his All-Pro years with the Jets, and it still showed up in Year 9.The position switch itself deserves more credit than it gets. Adams played linebacker for the first time in his professional life last season. Carroll was blunt about it. "[Carroll] straight up told me, 'You're going to be in the linebacker room, so get over it,'" Adams told the Raiders' website in August 2025. "So I was just like, 'Alright s--t, let's do it.'"He did it. And now the Vikings are betting that same adaptability carries into a new system.It's a fair question, and the honest answer is: probably, but in a limited capacity. The version of Jamal Adams who dominated as a blitzing safety for the Jets between 2017 and 2019 -- three Pro Bowls in four seasons, first-team All-Pro in 2019 -- is not walking through the door in Minnesota. That player was traded to Seattle for a package that included two first-round picks, a price that never paid off for the Seahawks.Injuries derailed nearly everything that followed. A torn labrum, a torn quad tendon, a hip injury -- Adams played just 34 games in four seasons with Seattle. He was released after the 2023 campaign, bounced through Tennessee and Detroit in 2024 without making much impact, and looked like a cautionary tale about big contracts and bad luck.But the Raiders gave him a real opportunity, and he stayed healthy for a full season for the first time in years. That's the clearest signal the Vikings are betting on. If Adams can stay on the field, Flores has the schematic creativity to find him snaps. Minnesota also drafted Jakobe Thomas in the third round, but third-round safeties are not guaranteed contributors in Year 1. Adams gives the team a bridge option who knows how to play under pressure.The real subplot here is Harrison Smith. The longtime Vikings safety hasn't officially announced retirement, and his decision -- whenever it comes -- will shape how much Minnesota actually relies on Adams. If Smith comes back, Adams is clear-cut depth. If Smith walks away for good, this signing suddenly looks like a quiet necessity dressed up as a low-risk flier.For a player entering his sixth team, the Vikings represent something straightforward -- a chance to be useful in a defence that needs exactly what he offers. Not a star turn. Not a redemption arc. Just a professional doing his job in a system built for him.
Article Summary: Jamal Adams is heading into his 10th NFL season. The Minnesota Vikings confirmed the signing of the veteran defensive back on July 27. Adams, 30, arrives having reinvented himself as a linebacker with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025, playing 448 snaps and showing enough to earn one more shot.

What's next for Hernández?

Elieser Hernández's stay in Atlanta ended the way a lot of veteran bullpen arms' stints do this time of year, fast and without ceremony. He threw three scoreless innings of relief in the Braves' 7-6 extra-innings win over Baltimore on Saturday, helping stretch that game out. A day later, Atlanta designated him for assignment, even as the club opened a series with the Mets at Citi Field.Hernández cleared waivers and was outrighted to Triple-A Gwinnett. He'd been through that process before, which meant he had the option to elect free agency rather than accept the assignment, and he took it. MLB.com's transactions log confirmed the move in blunt terms: "RHP Elieser Hernández elected free agency." His three innings against the Orioles are the only MLB innings he's logged in 2026.The DFA came despite a clean outing, which says more about Atlanta's roster math than about Hernández's stuff that day. He hadn't pitched in the majors since 2024, when he split time between Milwaukee and Los Angeles and posted a rough 15.2-inning stretch, 11 earned runs allowed and five home runs surrendered.Elieser Hernández contract details with the BravesPer Spotrac, Hernández signed a one-year, $850,000 deal with Atlanta, all of it guaranteed, with an average annual value matching the base salary.There was no signing bonus attached. His 2026 payroll figure for luxury tax purposes came in at $27,270, reflecting his buried roster status for most of the season.Career-wise, Hernández holds an 11-22 record with a 5.05 ERA across 100 games and 49 starts, spanning 306.1 innings with 287 strikeouts and a 1.32 WHIP. In his lone 2026 appearance, he went 1-0 with a 0.00 ERA over three innings, striking out two batters. The Venezuela-born right-hander, nicknamed "Lilo," debuted in the majors on May 10, 2018, after Miami took him in the first round of the 2013 draft.Hernández is now a free agent, cleared to sign with any of the league's 30 clubs. Whether he lands back in Atlanta's system or elsewhere, his next outing will be his first true audition since a shaky 2024. For a pitcher with a 5.05 career ERA looking to hang on, three scoreless innings is a start, not a guarantee.
Article Summary: Elieser Hernández threw three scoreless innings of relief in Atlanta's win over Baltimore. The Braves designated him for assignment and outrighted him to Triple-A Gwinnett. He elected free agency and can sign with any of the league's 30 clubs.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth: "When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat; instead, they…" - a timeless lesson on courage, perseverance and hope in difficult times
Article Text:
Queen Elizabeth

Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth II

"When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat; instead, they are all the more determined to struggle for a better future"

Exploring the true meaning of Queen Elizabeth’s quote

Why courage often shows up in small, everyday decisions

Why staying determined matters more than an immediate win

Why hope, in this quote, is something you actually do

How the Queen's own life reflected this idea

Why hardship can build genuine strength

How to actually use this idea day to day

Other memorable quotes by Queen Elizabeth

"Grief is the price we pay for love."

"It has always been easy to hate and destroy. To build and to cherish is much more difficult."

"We all need to get the balance right between action and reflection."

"It's worth remembering that it is often the small steps, not the giant leaps, that bring about the most lasting change."

What this quote means in today’s world

Everyone goes through periods when life feels genuinely hard, illness, money worries, loss, setbacks at work, moments when the future feels uncertain. The easy response is often to give up trying. Queen Elizabeth II offered a different way of thinking about those moments in her Christmas broadcast on the 25th of December 2008. "When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat," she said. "Instead, they are all the more determined to struggle for a better future." She was not pretending life is easy. She was simply describing what she believed made the difference between giving up and pushing on, a distinction she had plenty of occasion to think about across seven decades on the throne.The quote starts honestly, with "when life seems hard." There is no pretence here that difficulty is rare or that everyone avoids it. Everyone runs into stretches where progress feels painfully slow and obstacles seem too big to get past, whatever their circumstances happen to be.What follows is the actual point. Courage does not mean feeling no fear or no pain. It means refusing to let those feelings decide what happens next.The quote ends by pointing forward, towards "a better future," suggesting that hardship, faced properly, can actually sharpen someone's resolve rather than weaken it.People tend to picture courage as something dramatic, a single big moment of bravery. More often, it looks much smaller than that. Getting up and going back to work after a real disappointment. Asking for help during a genuinely hard time. Supporting a family through money troubles. Starting again after a business or a career falls apart. Continuing treatment through a long illness. None of these moments make headlines, yet each one takes the same basic quality, choosing to keep going anyway.A setback can feel like the end of the road, a rejected job application, a failed exam, a lost job, a broken relationship. In reality, most of these moments turn out to be turning points rather than final endings. Staying determined does not guarantee instant success. It simply keeps the door open for a future success that giving up would close for good. Someone who keeps learning and adjusting after a setback still has options that someone who quits no longer does.Hope often gets treated as just wishing things will get better on their own. This quote describes something more active. The courageous are "determined to struggle" for a better future, meaning hope only really means something once effort gets attached to it. Simply waiting for circumstances to improve is a very different thing from actually taking steps, however small, towards making that improvement happen.Elizabeth became heir to the throne during the turmoil of the Second World War and went on to reign through decades of huge social and political change. Her time as monarch included economic crises, constitutional disputes, terrorist attacks and, near the end of her reign, the Covid-19 pandemic. Across many of her speeches, she returned again and again to the same themes, endurance, duty, and the belief that difficulties can be overcome through shared effort and persistence. This particular quote fits that pattern closely.Nobody goes looking for suffering, yet difficult experiences do tend to build qualities that easier times rarely produce. Patience grows when progress is slow. Resilience develops through actually recovering from setbacks. Empathy deepens once someone has been through real struggle themselves, since it becomes much easier to recognise the same struggle in someone else. None of this glorifies hardship for its own sake. It simply recognises that adversity, met with real determination, can end up becoming a source of genuine strength rather than something that only leaves damage behind. The message reminds us that while hardship is never desirable, the character, wisdom and compassion forged through overcoming it can become some of life's most enduring strengths.Focus on the very next step rather than trying to solve the whole problem at once. Keep up routines that support your health, work and relationships, especially when things are difficult. Ask for support from family, friends or professionals rather than struggling entirely alone. Treat setbacks as something to learn from rather than proof that you have failed. And keep the long view in mind, since most difficult periods, however overwhelming they feel at the time, do eventually pass, even when it is genuinely hard to believe that while you are still in the middle of one.What makes this quote last is the balance it strikes. It never pretends suffering is not real, and it never promises every struggle will end quickly or easily. It simply offers a way of thinking about hard times, that courage is measured by the decision to keep pushing toward something better, even while the present moment still feels genuinely difficult. That is really the whole message packed into one sentence, and it explains why people keep returning to these words years after she first said them, long after the specific Christmas broadcast that produced them has been largely forgotten.
Article Summary: "When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat" Queen Elizabeth II said this in her Christmas broadcast on the 25th of December 2008. Courage does not mean feeling no fear or no pain, it means refusing to let those feelings decide what happens next.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Alexander the Great: "I am not afraid of an army of lions led by a sheep; I am afraid of…" - a timeless lesson on leadership, courage and the power of inspiring others
Article Text:
Alexander the Great (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Alexander the Great

"I am not afraid of an army of lions led by a sheep; I am afraid of an army of sheep led by a lion"

What is the meaning behind the quote by Alexander the Great

Why the idea still matters even without a confirmed source

Why talent on its own is rarely enough

Why confidence and courage tend to spread

Why this goes well beyond the battlefield

How to actually use this idea

Other quotes attributed to Alexander the Great

"There is nothing impossible to him who will try."

"I would rather excel others in the knowledge of what is excellent than in the extent of my power."

"Heaven cannot brook two suns, nor earth two masters."

“For my part, I think that to a man of spirit there is no other aim and end of his labours except the labours themselves.”

Why this still resonates today

Numbers and weapons matter in battle, but they are rarely the whole story. Sometimes the deciding factor is simply who is standing at the front, giving the orders. That idea sits behind one of the most famous lines connected to Alexander the Great. "I am not afraid of an army of lions led by a sheep; I am afraid of an army of sheep led by a lion," the quote goes. Whether or not Alexander himself actually said these exact words, the point behind them has clearly lasted, repeated across more than two thousand years of history, passed from one century to the next long after the man himself was gone. Armies have changed beyond recognition since then, replaced by boardrooms, classrooms and sports fields, yet the underlying question stays the same: does the person in charge bring out the best in people, or waste it?The quote works through two simple pictures. An army of lions represents individually brave, capable fighters. Even so, if the person leading them lacks judgement or nerve, all that individual strength can go to waste. An army of sheep represents ordinary people, not naturally fearless, yet capable of achieving far more than expected once a genuinely strong leader is guiding them.The point is straightforward. Leadership can completely change what a group of people is able to achieve together, sometimes mattering more than the raw talent sitting inside that group.Its enduring message is that vision, confidence and effective leadership have the power to inspire ordinary people to accomplish extraordinary things together.None of that uncertainty removes the value of the idea itself. A leader does far more than hand out instructions. They build a shared sense of purpose, give people something to trust in, and help a group stay focused when things get difficult. When people genuinely believe in whoever is leading them, they often start believing more in themselves too, and that shift alone can change what an entire group manages to achieve.Plenty of teams and organisations are stacked with talented people, yet talent without real direction can produce surprisingly inconsistent results. A skilled group with no coordination or shared purpose often struggles to reach anywhere near its actual potential. This is exactly why serious organisations invest heavily in developing leadership, not just technical skill, since the two rarely produce results on their own.People frequently take their emotional cues from whoever is leading them. A calm leader during a genuine crisis tends to calm everyone else down too. A leader who clearly believes in their team's ability often ends up creating that same belief inside the people being led. Confidence, in other words, is rarely just a private, individual trait. It moves through a group, usually starting from the top.Courage works in a similar way. It has never really meant an absence of fear, only the choice to act despite it. When a leader shows that kind of courage openly, it tends to give everyone else around them permission to do the same.Although this particular image comes from warfare, the underlying lesson clearly reaches much further. Teachers shape entire classrooms. Managers shape workplaces. Coaches shape how athletes perform under pressure. Parents shape families. In every one of these settings, the quality of leadership tends to shape how people respond to real challenges and real opportunities, whether or not a battle is involved anywhere.Lead by consistent example rather than by title or authority alone. Help build confidence in others, especially during genuinely difficult moments. Focus on developing the people around you rather than simply directing their tasks. Build trust the slow way, through consistency, rather than expecting it to appear automatically. And remember that leadership itself often decides how far a group's raw ability actually gets used.Leadership remains one of the most powerful forces inside any group, whatever the century. Technology keeps changing, and the challenges people face keep getting more complicated, yet people still respond strongly to leaders who inspire genuine confidence and give others a real sense of direction. This particular saying, whoever actually said it first, has survived over two thousand years for a simple reason. Ordinary people, guided well, can end up achieving things that look nothing short of extraordinary.
Article Summary: Leadership remains one of the most powerful forces inside any group. A leader does far more than hand out instructions. They build a shared sense of purpose, give people something to trust in, and help a group stay focused when things get difficult. Leadership can completely change what a group is able to achieve together.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Dave Bautista: "I'm a poor kid from the streets. What I've been able to achieve has really just been through hard work and…" - an inspiring lesson on resilience, self-belief and tu
Article Text:
Dave Bautista (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Dave Bautista

"I'm a poor kid from the streets. What I've been able to achieve has really just been through hard work and not letting anyone tell me that I couldn't do something. I always try to encourage people to just pursue your dreams"

What is the meaning behind Dave Bautista’s quote

Why where you start does not decide where you finish

The real story behind his career change

Why hard work stays essential even after talent gets you noticed

Why self-belief matters, especially when others doubt you

Why rejection rarely means the end of the road

Why pursuing a dream actually requires doing something

Other famous quotes by Dave Bautista

"I'm not afraid to go up to people and pick their brains and ask for advice. That's how you get better. That's how I've gotten better at everything I've ever done."

"I had been struggling to get roles in Hollywood for three and a half years after leaving the WWE. My agent turned me down three times before he even decided to take me on as a client."

"I was a poor kid. I came from nothing. We didn't have any money; a lot of times we didn't have any food. And now, all of a sudden, I'm a superhero in a Marvel movie. Talk about the American dream."

For some reason, I'm the guy people love to hate, which I think is weird. People who know me find that very strange, but for some reason, I am. I don't mind being that guy - I have fun with it.

Why this still matters today

Success stories tend to look simple from the outside. People see the awards, the fame, the money, but rarely the years of struggle and rejection that came first. Dave Bautista , the actor and former professional wrestler, is open about exactly that gap. "I'm a poor kid from the streets," he said. "What I've been able to achieve has really just been through hard work and not letting anyone tell me that I couldn't do something. I always try to encourage people to just pursue your dreams." He is not hiding where he started. He is pointing straight at it, treating his own difficult beginning as part of the story rather than something to keep quiet about once success arrived.Bautista begins by naming his own background honestly, "a poor kid from the streets," rather than glossing over it. What follows explains what he believes actually made the difference between staying stuck and getting somewhere, hard work paired with a flat refusal to accept other people's doubts as his own limits. The quote ends on encouragement, telling people to actually pursue their dreams rather than simply hold them at arm's length.People are born into very different circumstances, some with real financial security, others with poverty and instability from the beginning.Those differences are genuinely real and genuinely hard. What Bautista's own life shows is that a difficult start does not automatically decide the ending. Circumstances shape the path. They do not always control the destination.Bautista's shift from wrestling into acting was far from instant. He has openly described struggling to get roles in Hollywood for three and a half years after leaving WWE. His own current agent, the one who eventually took him on, actually turned him down three times before finally agreeing to represent him. That is not a story of overnight success. It is a story of getting rejected repeatedly and simply not stopping.He has also connected his childhood directly to where that persistence eventually led. "I was a poor kid. I came from nothing," he has said. "We didn't have any money; a lot of times we didn't have any food. And now, all of a sudden, I'm a superhero in a Marvel movie." That gap, between a childhood without enough food and a career playing one of the most recognisable characters in a global film franchise, is really the whole story his quote is trying to compress into a single sentence.Talent can open a door. It rarely keeps that door open by itself. Every serious achievement takes sustained effort over a long stretch of time, learning new skills, absorbing setbacks, improving after failure, and staying disciplined even when nothing seems to be moving. Bautista credits his own success to persistence rather than luck or natural advantage, and his own career backs that up directly.Doubt shows up from all directions throughout life, sometimes from strangers, sometimes from people much closer. The real danger is letting that doubt quietly become your own belief about yourself. Self-belief here does not mean assuming success is guaranteed. It means trusting that improvement is possible through real effort, which is exactly the refusal Bautista describes as central to his own career, the decision to keep going regardless of who along the way told him he could not.Nearly everyone who eventually succeeds gets rejected somewhere along the way. Actors lose auditions. Athletes miss out on teams. Entrepreneurs hear investors say no. Bautista's own agent said no to him three separate times before saying yes. Rejection, in his story, became something to push through rather than a signal to stop.Dreams give people direction. Actual effort is what turns that direction into something real. Plenty of people have ambitions. Considerably fewer keep working toward them consistently once the early excitement fades. Bautista's quote is not encouraging wishful thinking. It is encouraging the harder, less glamorous version, developing skills, absorbing criticism, and continuing even when the goal still feels far away.Modern culture tends to highlight the finished result while skipping past the struggle that actually produced it. Bautista's honesty about his own background offers something different, an actual account of where he started and what it took to get somewhere else entirely. His message matters most for anyone who feels boxed in by their own circumstances. Poverty, rejection and doubt can all create real obstacles. Article Title: CWG 2026: Why India's fastest man Gurindervir Singh crashed out despite finishing 2nd in his heat - explained
Article Text:
Gurindervir Singh (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)

NEW DELHI: India's fastest man Gurindervir Singh entered the Commonwealth Games carrying the weight of expectation after rewriting the national record earlier this year.Instead, his campaign came to an abrupt end in the men's 100m heats, with a hamstring injury emerging as the key reason behind his disappointing outing.The 25-year-old clocked 10.39 seconds to finish second in his heat, but the time was not enough to secure a place in the semifinals. Only the 17 fastest athletes across all 11 heats progressed, leaving Gurindervir 28th overall among 73 competitors.A time of 10.24 seconds would have been enough to advance.After the race, coach James Hillier revealed that the Indian sprinter had been battling a hamstring injury for the past month, something the team had deliberately kept under wraps.“Everyone will look at the timings and go why couldn't he do his best. He's had a hamstring injury for the last month, we've been keeping it quiet. Where he is at now, he can do the first 60m very well," Hillier said, as quoted by Nnis Sports.The injury explained the contrast between Gurindervir's recent form and his performance in Glasgow. In May, he became the first Indian man to break the 10.10-second barrier, clocking a national record 10.09 seconds at the Federation Cup in Ranchi.The run erased the previous mark of 10.15 seconds, set by Animesh Kujur just a day earlier, and established Gurindervir as one of India's brightest medal hopes heading into the Games.His early exit, however, dealt a setback to India's sprint ambitions.
Article Summary: India's fastest man Gurindervir Singh finishes second in men's 100m heats. The 25-year-old's time of 10.39 seconds was not enough to progress to the semifinals. Coach James Hillier revealed that the sprinter had been battling a hamstring injury for the past month.

Article Title: Why was former Minnesota Vikings Pro Bowler Everson Griffen arrested? Everything to know about the gross misdemeanor charge
Article Text:
Why was former Vikings Pro Bowler Everson Griffen arrested?(Getty)

Everson Griffen says arrest had nothing to do with drinking



Former Minnesota Vikings star Everson Griffen is back in the headlines, but this time it has nothing to do with football. The four-time Pro Bowler was arrested in Minnesota after police said he drove a vehicle that did not meet the restrictions tied to his driver's license.While the arrest raised fresh questions because of his past legal issues, authorities have not accused Griffen of driving under the influence in this case.According to a criminal complaint filed in Winona County, police stopped Everson Griffen at around 8 p.m. on July 23 after allegedly clocking his vehicle at 62 mph in a 40 mph zone on Riverview Drive in Winona, Minnesota. During the traffic stop, officers discovered that Griffen was driving a vehicle that allegedly did not have the ignition interlock device required under the terms of his restricted driver's license.An ignition interlock device requires a driver to provide a clean breath sample before a vehicle can start. Court records show Everson Griffen's driving privileges remain subject to that condition. Because the vehicle did not have the required system installed, officers arrested him on suspicion of violating his license restrictions. Prosecutors later charged him with a gross misdemeanor.He was released after posting bond and is scheduled to appear remotely in Winona County District Court on August 28.Soon after news of the arrest became public, Everson Griffen responded through a post on his Instagram account. He insisted the situation was an administrative issue and not a relapse."Nothing happened when I got pulled over last night. My license was revoked because I forgot to complete the required class/test, and I just moved, so I was planning to take care of both the class and the address change on Monday. I wasn't drinking, wasn't smoking, and wasn't doing anything wrong. Everything is fine."Everson Griffen shared that statement on Instagram shortly after his arrest. The criminal complaint adds another detail.According to court documents, an officer asked Griffen whether the required ignition interlock system was installed in the vehicle. The complaint says Griffen replied that he had taken the test to regain his license but failed it. A supervising officer then checked state records and confirmed that his license still carried the ignition interlock restriction.That point matters because the current case does not accuse Griffen of driving while impaired. Instead, it focuses on whether he violated the conditions attached to his restricted license. The arrest comes after a difficult stretch away from football. Griffen has spoken openly in recent months about rebuilding his life and recently said he was approaching one year of sobriety. He has also faced previous driving-related legal issues, including an impaired-driving conviction that led to the license restrictions. Local reports also said he received a citation in August 2025 after allegedly driving 130 mph in a 60 mph zone.Despite those off-field struggles, Griffen remains one of the most accomplished defensive players in Minnesota Vikings history. The Vikings selected him in the fourth round of the 2010 NFL Draft, and he spent 11 of his 12 NFL seasons with the franchise. He earned four Pro Bowl selections and finished his career with 88.5 sacks, including 85.5 with Minnesota.Now, the focus shifts to the courtroom. Griffen's Aug. 28 hearing will determine the next step in the case, while the former Vikings star continues to maintain that his arrest should not be mistaken for another alcohol-related incident.
Article Summary: Everson Griffen was arrested after police said he drove a vehicle that did not meet the restrictions tied to his driver's license. Authorities have not accused Griffen of driving under the influence in this case. He has also faced previous driving-related legal issues, including an impaired-driving conviction that led to the license restrictions.

Article Title: What the latest Baker Mayfield report really says about Tampa Bay's confidence in its $47 million franchise quarterback
Article Text:
Baker Mayfield (Getty Images)

Could the Buccaneers use the franchise tag instead of giving Baker Mayfield a new contract?

Baker Mayfield's contract situation in Tampa Bay is getting messier and more fascinating by the week. The Buccaneers quarterback is in the final year of a reworked deal worth $27 million in 2026, with no long-term extension anywhere close to the horizon. And now, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the franchise tag is emerging as a very real possibility for 2027 -- one that could cost Tampa Bay at least $47 million.A franchise tag has rarely been part of the public discussion around Mayfield's future, but Fowler believes it remains a realistic possibility."While Mayfield would prefer a long-term deal, he’s not afraid of the franchise tag, which would cost Tampa Bay at least $47M in 2027," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler wrote on his official X account on Sunday.From Mayfield's perspective, the financial risk appears limited. He has already earned significant money during his NFL career and is due another $40 million this season. That gives him room to be patient rather than force negotiations."Baker has made $131.8 million already in his career & he’ll make $40 million this season," Damage Inc. wrote on X on Sunday. "Getting tagged at $47 million at age 32 won’t faze him at all.I’m sure he would like another nine-digit contract, but he’s going to make over $200 million in his career regardless."While the financial side remains stable, Mayfield enters the season with something else to prove. Last year started in impressive fashion as both he and the Buccaneers looked like one of the NFL's biggest success stories through the first six weeks. That momentum faded quickly. Tampa Bay finished 8-9, missed the playoffs for the first time since 2019 and Mayfield's standing across the league took a hit.ESPN's annual survey of NFL executives, coaches and scouts reflected that shift. After previously being viewed among the league's top quarterbacks, Mayfield dropped out of the Top 10 and landed in the honourable mention category. He also missed out on the Pro Bowl after earning selections in each of his first two seasons with Tampa Bay.Even so, respect for his game has not disappeared. Mayfield was the only quarterback from the NFC South to receive votes in the rankings."Mayfield is a winner," one anonymous NFL coordinator told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. "He can make every throw. Fearless. Teammates seem to love to play for him."Mayfield himself has made it clear that contract talks are not his immediate focus, even if discussions have not progressed as hoped."(Contract extension talks) not anywhere close to what we were thinking," Mayfield told Tampa Bay Times NFL reporter Rick Stroud. "Would love to be here long term, but as of right now that’s not exactly the case. But I’m under contract for 2026. The guys in that locker room, the staff know that I’m still gonna be me. I’m still going to do everything I can to help this team win a Super Bowl. To me, that’s the priority. Everything else will take care of itself. "For now, the Buccaneers do not appear under pressure to make an immediate decision. A strong 2026 season could strengthen Mayfield's case for another long-term deal. If not, the franchise tag offers Tampa Bay another option while keeping its starting quarterback in place.
Article Summary: Baker Mayfield is in the final year of a reworked deal worth $27 million in 2026. The franchise tag is emerging as a very real possibility for 2027. Mayfield has made $131.8 million already in his career and is due $40 million this season.

Article Title: "Not all details from the accident are being shared": Kyle Shanahan car crash mystery deepens as police refuse to release key details after two weeks of silence
Article Text:
kyle shanahan (Getty Images)

Why are officials not revealing more about Kyle Shanahan's car accident?

Kyle Shanahan's absence has become one of the biggest storylines as the San Francisco 49ers opened training camp, but not because of football. The head coach is recovering from serious injuries suffered in a car crash earlier this month, leaving the organisation without its leader during an important stage of pre-season preparations. While the team has disclosed the extent of Shanahan's injuries, several details surrounding the accident remain undisclosed, adding fresh questions as the 49ers balance optimism over his recovery with uncertainty over when he can fully return.The 49ers confirmed that the accident took place on July 14, 2026, near Shanahan's home in Los Altos Hills, California. The collision happened at a busy intersection near Alma Street and Hamilton Avenue on the western edge of downtown Palo Alto, where emergency crews responded after a black Tesla and a blue Mercedes SUV crashed.Shanahan suffered extensive injuries. He sustained a concussion, broke his nose, hand and three ribs, and required 40 stitches to his face. The team also revealed that he continues to experience concussion-like symptoms, preventing him from taking part in training camp for now.Even with those medical updates, much about the crash remains unclear.San Francisco Chronicle reporter Eric Branch highlighted the limited information available, writing: “Kyle Shanahan badly injured in car crash and has ongoing concussion symptoms as camp begins.Not all details from the accident are being shared. ‘There will be no information released regarding the cause of the collision or who was at fault.'”That statement came from Lt. Nicholas Martinez, who confirmed that both drivers remained at the scene and fully cooperated with investigators. Authorities also said no citations were issued and there was no indication that either driver was impaired.General manager John Lynch acknowledged that Shanahan is still focused on his recovery rather than football.“He’s not ready yet to be talking to you guys. He’s not ready to be talking to our team.”Lynch, however, expressed confidence that the situation is moving in the right direction and expects Shanahan to be back well before the regular season begins.“But you know, just like we talked about with players, the timeline kind of takes care of itself. So he’s got to meet certain markers. But I think the expectation is that long before that, it’ll be better.”That recovery now carries added importance for San Francisco. The 49ers battled through a string of injuries during the 2025 season yet remained competitive and kept themselves in the playoff conversation. Article Title: Why was Isaiah Rider arrested? Former Lakers star is in police custody in a case related to his wife Vanessa
Article Text:
Isaiah Rider. Image via: Getty Images

Former NBA champion Isaiah Rider arrested, again

What happened to Isaiah Rider?

Is Isaiah Rider's latest arrest related to his wife Vanessa?

Isaiah Rider was arrested again Thursday night, his third arrest in less than two months, this time on a misdemeanor charge for failing to comply with a court order. Maricopa County jail records show the former NBA Slam Dunk champion was booked Friday morning, pleaded guilty, and is expected to remain in custody until Tuesday.The charge traces back to a protective order his estranged wife, Vanessa, obtained last year. Rider, 55, has now been arrested twice before in connection with that same order, and the latest booking keeps a messy divorce and custody dispute firmly in public view.This is not new territory for Rider. He was picked up twice in December, first for allegedly violating the protective order and then again days later for skipping a hearing on whether that order should stay in place.A judge extended it after Vanessa showed up and Rider did not.Thursday's arrest follows the same pattern, a court-related misdemeanor rather than a new allegation of contact or violence, per TMZ . Police records describe it simply as a failure to comply with a court order, and the guilty finding suggests Rider did not contest it once he was in front of a judge.The former fifth overall pick in the 1993 NBA Draft spent nine seasons in the league, three years apiece with the Minnesota Timberwolves and Portland Trail Blazers before single seasons with the Atlanta Hawks, Los Angeles Lakers and Denver Nuggets.He won the Slam Dunk Contest as a rookie in 1994 and picked up a championship ring in 2001, even though he did not make the Lakers' playoff roster that year.The trouble began last year when Vanessa filed for a protective order, alleging Rider had been hostile toward her on multiple occasions. Court documents describe threatening language directed at her and their teenage son. Rider has denied the allegations and pointed instead to the timing of his own divorce filing in November 2024, arguing the order followed shortly after he moved to end the marriage.The order barred Rider from contacting Vanessa or their son and from going near the family home or the boy's school. Rider has claimed in filings that he did not receive the paperwork until December, weeks after it was granted in July.He was arrested that same month for allegedly violating the order, then arrested again for missing the hearing on whether it should be extended. Vanessa appeared for that hearing. The judge sided with her and kept the order in place, setting up the conditions that led to Thursday's arrest.Yes, at least indirectly. Thursday's booking was not for a new incident involving Vanessa but for failing to comply with a court order that exists because of her original petition, which makes this arrest part of the same unresolved case rather than a separate legal matter.Vanessa has been consistent about her reasons for seeking the order in the first place. "The Order of Protection was sought and granted solely for safety reasons, to protect myself and my child from further harm," she said in a statement , adding that she views the process as necessary rather than tactical and has asked the public to respect the privacy of a case involving a minor.
Article Summary: Isaiah Rider was arrested again Thursday night, this time on a misdemeanor charge for failing to comply with a court order. The charge traces back to a protective order his estranged wife, Vanessa, obtained last year. Rider, 55, has now been arrested twice before in connection with that same order.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind” - How Rafael Nadal’s fam
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind” - How Rafael Nadal’s family stood by him through every injury on his road to tennis immortality (Image via Getty)

How did Rafael Nadal overcome a career-threatening foot condition?

Why did Rafael Nadal always choose family and home over fame?

What did Rafael Nadal say about his wife and family during his injury battles?

What life lesson did Rafael Nadal learn from pain and defeat?

For years, Rafael Nadal inspired fans with his fight on the tennis court. What many people did not see was the battle he fought away from the spotlight. Long before becoming a 22-time Grand Slam champion, Nadal was told that a rare foot condition could end his career. He dealt with constant pain, serious injuries and doubts about whether he could keep playing. Yet he kept coming back. While his determination made headlines, Nadal has always said his biggest strength was the people who stood beside him. Their support helped him survive the hardest moments and build one of the greatest careers in tennis history.In 2005, Nadal won his first French Open title at just 19 years old. Soon after that breakthrough, he was diagnosed with Mueller-Weiss syndrome, a rare condition that affects the bones in the foot.Doctors warned that continuing his career at the highest level might not be possible.Instead of giving up, Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca. There, he was surrounded by his father Sebastián, mother Ana María, sister Maribel and his longtime partner Mery Perelló. Their support gave him the strength to keep moving forward when his future looked uncertain.Looking back on those difficult years, Nadal once said:“Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible.They give me peace of mind.”Despite becoming one of the biggest names in world sport, Nadal never left the place where he grew up. He stayed close to his family in Manacor and continued living the simple life that had shaped him from childhood.His uncle and longtime coach Toni Nadal taught him to stay humble, respect opponents and never believe he was bigger than the game. Those lessons stayed with him throughout his career.Nadal has often explained that returning home helped him switch off from the pressure of professional tennis. In Manacor, he was simply Rafa, spending time with friends and family. That normal life became an important part of maintaining his mental balance through the highs and lows of the sport.Nadal’s wife, Mery “Xisca” Perelló, was by his side long before he became a global star. She witnessed every comeback, every rehabilitation session and every painful setback that fans rarely saw.As injuries continued in the final years of his career, those shared sacrifices became even more meaningful. With his wife, young son and team watching from the stands, Nadal reflected on everything they had gone through together.He said:“Having my family here, my wife, my son, my team… it’s emotional because they know how hard the process has been. They have been through the good moments, but especially the tough moments during all these years of injuries.”Nadal never believed success came without suffering. Throughout his career, he played through injuries, long matches and physical pain that would have stopped many athletes. Instead of running from those challenges, he accepted them as part of the journey.That mindset became one of the biggest reasons behind his remarkable career.As Nadal explained:“If you don’t lose, you cannot enjoy the victories. You have to accept both things. I learned during my career to enjoy suffering.”His story goes far beyond Grand Slam trophies or records. It shows that true strength is not only about winning titles but also about staying grounded when life becomes difficult. Through every injury and every comeback, Nadal never lost sight of the people who mattered most. Their love gave him the peace, confidence and support to keep chasing his dreams, making his journey one of the most inspiring stories in modern sport.
Article Summary: Rafael Nadal was diagnosed with a career-threatening foot condition in 2005. Doctors told him it could end his career, but he refused to give up. Instead of giving up, Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca. There, he was surrounded by his father, mother and sister. Their support gave him the strength to keep moving forward when his future looked uncertain.

Article Title: North Carolina spent 25 years rebuilding an elk population that had disappeared from the state; in 2027, it will allow its first limited hunt with just two permits
Article Text:
Elk were once found across much of North Carolina but disappeared from the state many years ago

The hunt

Elk in western North Carolina. (Photos: WLOS)

The permits

The rules

For the first time since elk were reintroduced to western North Carolina 25 years ago, the state will allow a limited elk hunting season. The decision comes after wildlife officials said the elk population has recovered enough to support controlled hunting while continuing conservation efforts.The change follows the signing of House Bill 747 by North Carolina Governor Josh Stein on July 7. The law allows the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission (NCWRC) to issue two elk hunting permits during the 2027 hunting season.Officials say the move is not aimed at reducing the population quickly but is part of a long-term wildlife management plan. The money raised through the permits will also be used for elk conservation and management.Elk once lived across large parts of North Carolina but disappeared from the state after years of overhunting and habitat loss. About 25 years ago, wildlife agencies began reintroducing the animals to western North Carolina. Since then, the population has gradually recovered and become stable.According to Justin McVey, district wildlife biologist with the NCWRC, the state has now reached an important milestone."Our goal for elk management in the state is to have a sustainable huntable population and at this point we've reached that goal," McVey said, as quoted by ABC 13 news.A sustainable population means there are enough animals to maintain healthy numbers while also allowing a limited number to be hunted without affecting the long-term survival of the species.The state is taking a cautious approach by issuing only two permits during the first hunting season. The two permits will be distributed in different ways.One permit will be auctioned through a wildlife conservation non-profit organisation that took part in the elk reintroduction programme in North Carolina.Under the law, the selected non-profit can keep up to 25% of the auction proceeds. The remaining money will go towards wildlife conservation.The second permit will be issued through a public raffle. Raffle tickets will cost $20 each, and participants can buy up to 30 tickets for $500. To enter, buyers must have a valid North Carolina hunting licence or be eligible for a licence exemption under state regulations.The Wildlife Resources Commission may receive up to $25,000 from the raffle proceeds. The rest of the money collected from both the auction and raffle will be deposited into the state's Wildlife Resources Fund, where it will be used for elk conservation and management programmes.McVey said the permits are expected to become available in July 2027. The elk hunting season is scheduled to begin later that year in October.Hunters who receive permits will be allowed to hunt in areas within the state's designated elk zone where elk are present."They'll be able to basically hunt any area in the elk zone that has elk; it'll be private land as well as game lands," McVey said.However, anyone planning to hunt on private property must first obtain permission from the landowner.Wildlife officials also said hunters must follow all state hunting regulations. Anyone found violating the rules could face fines or other legal penalties.In addition, every elk harvested during the season must be reported to the NCWRC and presented to the agency as required under the new law.
Article Summary: North Carolina will allow a limited elk hunting season for the first time since elk were reintroduced to western North Carolina 25 years ago. Officials say the move is not aimed at reducing the population quickly but is part of a long-term wildlife management plan. Money raised through the permits will also be used for elk conservation and management.

Article Title: Archaeologists uncover rare 2,000-year-old Liubo game boards in Han Dynasty tombs, but its rules remain one of history's greatest mysteries
Article Text:
Image: AI Generated

Rare Liubo game boards discovered inside Han Dynasty tombs

What was Liubo, and why are its rules still unknown

Archaeology suggests Liubo was played at banquets as well as in tombs

Why Liubo remains one of archaeology's greatest unsolved puzzles

Centuries before chess spread across Asia, another board game captivated people throughout ancient China. Known as Liubo, it was played by emperors, nobles and ordinary families during the Han Dynasty, appearing so frequently that complete game sets were buried alongside the dead. Yet despite its popularity more than 2,000 years ago, the game's rules have almost entirely vanished. A recent archaeological discovery of rare Liubo game boards carved into Han Dynasty tombs has renewed interest in one of China's greatest historical mysteries. The find not only highlights the game's importance in everyday life and burial traditions but also underscores a remarkable paradox: archaeologists know what the board looked like, what pieces players used and where the game was played, yet no one can say with certainty how a match actually unfolded.Archaeologists identified two Liubo boards engraved directly onto square bricks inside Han Dynasty tombs dating to around 2,000 years ago. The discovery formed part of a larger excavation that also revealed pottery figurines, ceramic vessels and other funerary objects.Although Liubo boards have been discovered before, archaeologists rarely find them preserved in their original burial context. Their placement inside tombs suggests the game held lasting significance beyond recreation.During the Han Dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), objects interred with the deceased often reflected activities or possessions considered valuable in the afterlife.Evidence from the Metropolitan Museum of Art supports this interpretation. Its well-preserved Liubo Board and Pieces, dating from the 1st century BCE–1st century CE, includes gaming pieces made from earthenware and bone. The museum notes that Liubo was "a popular game in the Han dynasty" and that such sets embodied wishes for the continuation of life after death.Liubo emerged no later than the Warring States period and remained one of China's most widely played board games for several centuries before gradually disappearing after the Han Dynasty.Players competed on a square board decorated with a distinctive TLV pattern, using gaming pieces and throwing six casting sticks or, in some versions, dice, to determine movement. Beyond these basic elements, certainty quickly disappears.In his influential study, ‘ A Tricky Game: A Re-evaluation of Liubo Based on Archaeological and Textual Evidence ,’ Dr Armin Selbitschka of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich argues that modern scholarship has often overstated the game's supposed mystical or divinatory nature. After examining archaeological discoveries alongside surviving historical texts, he concludes that Liubo was primarily a game of entertainment, even though symbolic and religious associations emerged in certain regions during the later Eastern Han period.Crucially, no ancient instruction manual explaining the rules has survived. Historians have proposed several reconstructions based on excavated boards, gaming pieces and literary references, but none has achieved scholarly consensus. As a result, Liubo remains one of the few major ancient board games whose equipment is well documented while its gameplay remains largely unknown.The new discovery fits a broader archaeological pattern seen across Han Dynasty China. Selbitschka's research examined dozens of excavated tombs containing Liubo equipment and found that game boards frequently appeared alongside food vessels, drinking cups, musical instruments and figurines. Rather than representing isolated ritual objects, these groupings resemble scenes of banquets and social gatherings recreated inside tombs.The study argues that Liubo occupied an important place in elite entertainment. Historical writings by authors such as Sima Qian also refer to the game in descriptions of court life, competitions and leisure, reinforcing archaeological evidence that it was a familiar pastime rather than an obscure ceremonial practice.This interpretation contrasts with older theories that viewed Liubo mainly as a tool for divination because of the board's distinctive TLV design. According to Selbitschka, archaeological evidence indicates that recreational play remained its principal role throughout most of the Western Han period.Few ancient games present such an unusual challenge to historians. Archaeologists have uncovered exquisitely crafted lacquered boards, ceramic playing pieces, bronze fittings, carved stone examples and complete Liubo sets from royal mausoleums, aristocratic burials and Han Dynasty tombs across China. Museums, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, preserve these remarkable artefacts. Paintings, stone reliefs and funerary objects even depict people gathered around Liubo boards, confirming that it was far more than an obscure pastime.A carved board inside a Han Dynasty tomb or a complete gaming set recovered from an ancient burial may appear modest compared with spectacular treasures of gold or jade, yet each provides another clue about a game that dominated Chinese society for centuries before disappearing almost completely by the end of the Tang Dynasty. Future excavations may eventually uncover an illustrated manual, an inscribed game board or a more detailed written account capable of solving the mystery.Until then, Liubo remains one of archaeology's most intriguing unsolved puzzles. It is a rare example of a game whose equipment, artwork and cultural significance have survived for more than two millennia, while the knowledge required to play it has quietly slipped out of history.
Article Summary: Rare Liubo game boards discovered inside Han Dynasty tombs. Archaeologists identified two Liubos engraved directly onto square bricks. The discovery formed part of a larger excavation that also revealed pottery figurines, ceramic vessels and other funerary objects. The find highlights the game's importance in everyday life.

Article Title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon shared the story of almost dying in March 2020; says: I told my wife to call the company and tell them ...
Article Text:
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said he “nearly died” from heart failure

Jamie Dimon recalls Citigroup exit

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has revealed about the time he nearly died in March 2020 after suffering an aortic dissection, a serious condition that required emergency open-heart surgery. Speaking on The Master Investor Podcast, host Wilfred Frost asked Jamie Dimon about the time he nearly died in March 2020 after suffering an aortic dissection, a serious condition that required emergency open-heart surgery. Dimon said he immediately understood how dangerous the situation was because many people with the condition do not survive long enough to reach or leave the hospital."I knew at that point in time that you know there might be goodbye," Dimon said. He recalled asking his wife to contact the company immediately. "I told my wife, call the company and tell them exactly what's happening so they can do what they got to do," he said.During the interview, Jamie Dimon said that there were moments in his life when he came close to walking away from Wall Street altogether. Dimon also spoke about another turning point in his career — being fired as president of Citigroup in 1998.He said he was called into a meeting with Sandy Weill and John Reed and was asked to resign because of organisational changes. The decision came as a surprise and left him confused.After returning home, he told his family the news. He recalled that his youngest daughter asked whether they would now have to "sleep on the streets."Despite the setback, Dimon said he never allowed the job loss to define him. "It affected my net worth, not my self-worth," he said.He also remembered that about 50 senior Citibank managers came to his apartment to say goodbye, a gesture that stayed with him.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said he nearly died in March 2020 after suffering an aortic dissection, a serious condition that required emergency open-heart surgery. Dimon also spoke about another turning point in his career — being fired as president of Citigroup in 1998.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.

Article Title: Man booked for sexually assaulting and injuring stray dog in Navi Mumbai
